_why: queue archive (2026-11-24): every queue in Review's queue list carries an archive button beside its name
queue archive (2026-11-24): the Jobs page carries an 'Archived queues' block - its table, or its empty state on a database with nothing archived

queue archive (2026-11-24): archiving a queue from the list takes it out of the list and says where it went; the Jobs page lists it first among the archived (newest first) with Restore to Review, which puts it back. It archives the SECOND queue listed, never the one on screen, and waits for the list to re-read before leaving, so no read is cut off mid-flight. Archives and restores one queue of the sandbox copy (net no change), so it sorts late

actions.eval: async () => { const rows = () => document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="queue-picker"] [data-testid^="queue-row-"]'); const n0 = rows().length; const btns = document.querySelectorAll('[data-testid="queue-picker"] [data-testid^="queue-archive-"]'); if (btns.length < 2) throw new Error('need two queues in the list to archive one that is not on screen, have ' + btns.length); btns[1].click(); for (let i = 0; i < 300; i++) { const toast = [...document.querySelectorAll('.toast')].some(t => t.textContent.includes('Jobs › Archived queues')); if (toast && rows().length === n0 - 1) return; await new Promise(r => setTimeout(r, 200)) } throw new Error('the archived queue did not leave the list within 60 s') }
